chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Ala' the seller of al-Sabiri, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who deposited wealth with a man, and when death approached her, she said to him, 'The wealth that I gave you is for so-and-so.' Then the woman died, and her heirs came to the man and said to him, 'Our companion had wealth which we see only with you, so swear to us that we have nothing with you.' He said, 'If she was trustworthy with him, let him swear; and if she was suspected (of owing more), he should not swear, and the matter rests on what it was, for she is entitled to one-third of her wealth.'

key_terms.مُتَّهَمَةً: Suspected (implies she owed more than stated)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on inherited deposited wealth when the original depositor's instructions are unclear?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the evidentiary standards for heirs claiming deposited wealth (*wadi'ah*) when the depositor dies without a detailed inventory. It establishes that if the depositor is deemed trustworthy (*ma'mun*), the heirs are entitled to one-third of the total amount held, reflecting the presumption of partial retention; however, if she is suspected (*muttahamah*), the depositor's oath determines the exact liability, illustrating the Shia juristic principle of balancing presumption of ownership with the reliability of the witness.
